subject.title: [Bug] QQ Bot: skill_workshop approval "Allow" button always recorded as rejected

question: Should a QQ C2C approval callback grant authority solely because it came from a direct conversation, or must the callback actor still match an explicit approver or owner identity?
rationale: Current behavior deliberately separates permission to DM the bot from permission to approve sensitive operations, while the linked PR would collapse those boundaries for every direct conversation.

options.title: Require explicit approval identity
options.body: Keep the current fail-closed default and resolve C2C approvals only when the callback actor matches configured approvers, owner identity, or canonical command authorization.

options.title: Trust every C2C sender
options.body: Accept all direct-conversation approval callbacks, including senders admitted by an open wildcard DM policy, and explicitly own the broader authorization boundary.

options.title: Add an opt-in C2C policy
options.body: Preserve explicit authorization by default but introduce a documented QQ-specific setting for operators who intentionally trust all direct-message senders.

recommendation.title: Require explicit approval identity
recommendation.body: Keep the current fail-closed default and resolve C2C approvals only when the callback actor matches configured approvers, owner identity, or canonical command authorization.

likelyOwner.reason: They reviewed and merged the current authorization contract and carried the latest substantive fixups on this exact QQ approval path.
